Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).
This version should be easier to implement and explain to users.

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

With the current design (swap full msg.value → USDC, then refund excess in USDC), the contract simply doesn’t have a path to refund ETH.

Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).
